text:
It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award.
He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of the season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup.
This week at Galatasaray’s Rams Park, however, Garnacho, who in the summer signed on loan for Villa after a season at Chelsea, was nowhere to be seen. Villa, per competition rules, were permitted to name a dozen substitutes but Unai Emery named only 11. Garnacho did not travel and was again conspicuous by his absence, left out of the matchday squad for the third successive game. He has played only 95 minutes across seven games in all competitions, 34 across four league outings. He is yet to start for Villa and his last appearance was a three-minute cameo against Fulham at the end of last month. Welcome to The Curious Case of Alejandro Garnacho.
It is happening again, isn’t it? Last season it was Harvey Elliott who was left out in the cold for the season after signing on loan from Liverpool and now it is Garnacho on the periphery. On Wednesday it emerged Garnacho has wiped all trace of Villa from his Instagram account, the latest nadir for a talented player once the recipient of gushing compliments, and the ultimate telltale sign of a deteriorating relationship. Will Garnacho still be at Villa post-January? Villa halted Elliott’s game time to avoid triggering a permanent transfer and it appears they are doing similar with Garnacho, whom they have a conditional obligation to buy for about £43m. It is thought the buy option relates to appearances but, unlike the Elliott deal, the details remain a secret.
At this point it is important to remember the power structure at Villa. In short: Emery has the run of the place, great autonomy, and further control is pending with the Basque expected to sign a new long-term contract. Emery decides which players come in the door and he pushed for Garnacho’s signing. The president of football operations and de facto sporting director, Roberto Olabe, helps make Emery’s wishes come true. When Garnacho joined Villa in July, Emery expressed delight: “He is so talented … we are really happy.” So, what has changed?
The picture has shifted since the start of October. Emery and his staff felt there were green shoots during the extended international break, in which Garnacho scored in friendlies against Southampton and Sevilla. As one of the players not on international duty, he had the chance to get up to speed during Villa’s warm-weather camp in Spain. “He is getting better and for him the two weeks we worked were very important,” was Emery’s take. “He is working well and progressing.”
Or at least that was the thought. He has been omitted from four of Villa’s past five league squads. Garnacho is believed to have been training professionally but after Saturday’s stalemate with Sunderland, Emery suggested the 22-year-old was a long way from featuring. “I am trying to select the players I think that are ready to play,” Villa’s manager said to a question about the absences of Tammy Abraham, Lamare Bogarde and Garnacho. It was damning, then, that Abraham and Bogarde were on the bench for Tuesday’s defeat. When asked whether Garnacho was fit, Emery did not dress things up. “I think the players here are the best players to be with us,” he replied.
It is all the more perplexing given the chances – and goals – have dried up. Villa have failed to score in four of their past six matches – their four goals at Manchester United, whom the table tells us are the second-worst team in the division, represent an anomaly on this run – and Emery acknowledges they are not producing enough offensively. How low is Garnacho in the pecking order if he cannot make the bench? Johan Manzambi, Alysson, Emiliano Buendía, John McGinn, Ibrahim Mbaye and George Hemmings are in front of him.
A campaign that got off to a bad start for Garnacho – he missed the Super Cup in August owing to a concussion sustained in a friendly in Thailand – has never got off the ground. It is hard to believe a player bought by Chelsea for £40m has nothing to offer and easy to forget Garnacho made 43 appearances last season, 24 in the top flight, including 14 starts. By this point last year, he had started five Premier League games, two in the Champions League and another in the Carabao Cup. It is a year to the day since he began Chelsea’s 3-0 win over Barcelona. At the same time Garnacho was not a regular and Chelsea, who did summer deals with Villa to buy Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martínez and sell Nicolas Jackson, were happy for him to depart.
A slow start under Emery would be nothing new – just ask Youri Tielemans who became undroppable – but none of the noises generate belief that the winger could yet prove a slow-burning success. Four months in, is this the beginning of the end? The former Villa striker Gabriel Agbonlahor raised a series of legitimate questions on TalkSport amid a backdrop of ticket-price hikes for the fifth straight year and the battle to meet financial regulations. “What are you wasting on wages? What are you wasting on loan fee?” he asked. Perhaps the most pertinent question talked to the bigger picture. “What player is going to want to come on loan to Aston Villa?”
